statements.statement: A while loop that never updates its counter variable will run forever.
statements.explanation: If the counter never changes, the condition never becomes false, so the loop never stops. This is the most common cause of infinite loops.

statements.statement: while (true) { } will eventually stop on its own once it has run enough times.
statements.explanation: while (true) never stops on its own because the condition true can never become false. You must manually kill the program with Ctrl + C.

statements.statement: An infinite loop is always caused by using while (true).
statements.explanation: Infinite loops can also happen when you forget to update a counter, or when the condition is written in a way that can never become false. while (true) is just one example.

statements.statement: If your program freezes and stops responding, a runaway loop is a likely cause.
statements.explanation: An infinite loop consumes all available processing time, making the program appear frozen. It is one of the first things to check when a program hangs.
